doc.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022

title: New Yorker blurb about her
summary: Rowe reads a New Yorker piece praising her; she is delighted, having never been mentioned there before.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Okay. I’d like to read a paragraph here and perhaps you have a comment or reaction to it. This is from Steve Fudderman who wrote for “Night Life.”
I was so happy. Go ahead.

Okay. It says, “With few guarantees of either recognition or fortune, the life of a serious jazz instrumentalist is a saga of fortitude. Virginia Mayhew, a post-bop saxophonist and composer of obvious depth and feeling has bobbed and weaved through the musical trenches for four decades now, accruing respect from her peers and offering pleasure to those who have become acquainted with her artistry.” And then it goes on to say your upcoming gig at Small’s, which “helps keep the heart of mainstream jazz beating, much like Mayhew herself.”

Wow. You know I sent him a message immediately because for two reasons. First of all he totally gets it, and second of all because all the years that I’ve been here I’ve never gotten mentioned in the New Yorker. And it’s like, it’s not really a big deal obviously but I was so happy. And I have a friend who’s 94 and she gets the New Yorker and she’s always reading it, and finally she saw my name there with a good little blurb so it was wonderful on so many levels.
I hope you cut it out, because I would have.

Well I have it on my computer. Maybe I’ll print it up so I’ll have a back-up copy. But that was just — I was so happy to get that. I’ve had a few things like that happen in the last year or so. It’s — ah — just when you need it, a little, somebody gets it and it really, the timing has been good.
